## Overview

This document describes how the street intersection dataset for Cook County was created. Intersections were derived from OpenStreetMap (OSM) road data in four steps:

1. Clip a statewide OSM extract to Cook County.
2. Filter the roads to the drivable street network.
3. Build a street network graph and merge nearby nodes into single intersection points.
4. Assign each intersection to a study-area unit (Chicago community area or suburban municipality).

All processing is done locally on a downloaded OSM file, so no online map service (Overpass API) is queried. The implementation code is in [`dataprep.html`](dataprep.html) (*Street Intersections*); the code below summarizes it.

## Software

- **osmium-tool** (1.16), installed from conda-forge into the `osmnx-env` conda environment, for clipping and filtering OSM files.
- **OSMnx** (2.1), a Python package, for building the street graph and identifying intersections.
- **R** with `sf` and `reticulate`, which runs the osmium and OSMnx steps and handles the spatial join.

```r
reticulate::conda_install("osmnx-env", packages = "osmium-tool", channel = "conda-forge")
reticulate::use_condaenv("osmnx-env", required = TRUE)
ox <- reticulate::import("osmnx", convert = FALSE)
```

## Step 1 — Clip OSM Data to Cook County

The Illinois OSM extract (`illinois-latest.osm.pbf`) was downloaded from [GeoFabrik](https://download.geofabrik.de/north-america/us/illinois.html). The Cook County boundary (U.S. Census TIGER/Line) was saved as GeoJSON in longitude/latitude (EPSG:4326), and `osmium extract` was used to keep only the OSM data inside the county.

```r
cc_boundary_geo <- st_read("data/boundaries/cc_boundary.shp") |> st_transform(4326)
st_write(cc_boundary_geo, "data/boundaries/cc_boundary.geojson", delete_dsn = TRUE)

reticulate::conda_run2(
  cmd = "osmium",
  args = c(
    "extract", "--polygon", "data/boundaries/cc_boundary.geojson",
    "data/osm/illinois-latest.osm.pbf",
    "-o", "data/osm/cook_extract.osm.pbf", "--overwrite"
  ),
  envname = "osmnx-env"
)
```

## Step 2 — Filter to the Drivable Street Network

The Cook County extract was filtered with `osmium tags-filter` in five passes. The first pass keeps road types used by vehicles; the remaining passes remove roads that should not count as street intersections.

| Pass | Rule | OSM tags |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Keep drivable road types | `highway` = primary, primary_link, secondary, secondary_link, tertiary, tertiary_link, trunk, trunk_link, residential, unclassified, service, busway, construction, corridor |
| 2 | Remove parking aisles and driveways | `service` = parking_aisle, driveway |
| 3 | Remove private roads | `access` = private |
| 4 | Remove airport features | any `aeroway` tag |
| 5 | Remove indoor ways | `indoor` = yes |

Motorways (`highway=motorway`) are not included. The last pass writes the result as an OSM XML file (`cook_drive_network.osm`), the format OSMnx reads in Step 3.

```r
# 1. Keep drivable road types
reticulate::conda_run2(
  cmd = "osmium",
  args = c(
    "tags-filter", "data/osm/cook_extract.osm.pbf",
    "w/highway=primary,primary_link,unclassified,residential,secondary,secondary_link,service,tertiary,tertiary_link,trunk,trunk_link,busway,construction,corridor",
    "-o", "data/osm/cook_01_highway.osm.pbf", "--overwrite"
  ),
  envname = "osmnx-env"
)

# 2. Remove parking aisles and driveways
reticulate::conda_run2(
  cmd = "osmium",
  args = c(
    "tags-filter", "-i", "data/osm/cook_01_highway.osm.pbf",
    "w/service=parking_aisle,driveway",
    "-o", "data/osm/cook_02_service.osm.pbf", "--overwrite"
  ),
  envname = "osmnx-env"
)

# 3. Remove private roads
reticulate::conda_run2(
  cmd = "osmium",
  args = c(
    "tags-filter", "-i", "data/osm/cook_02_service.osm.pbf",
    "w/access=private",
    "-o", "data/osm/cook_03_access.osm.pbf", "--overwrite"
  ),
  envname = "osmnx-env"
)

# 4. Remove airport features
reticulate::conda_run2(
  cmd = "osmium",
  args = c(
    "tags-filter", "-i", "data/osm/cook_03_access.osm.pbf",
    "w/aeroway",
    "-o", "data/osm/cook_04_aeroway.osm.pbf", "--overwrite"
  ),
  envname = "osmnx-env"
)

# 5. Remove indoor ways; write OSM XML for OSMnx
reticulate::conda_run2(
  cmd = "osmium",
  args = c(
    "tags-filter", "-i", "data/osm/cook_04_aeroway.osm.pbf",
    "w/indoor=yes",
    "-o", "data/osm/cook_drive_network.osm", "-f", "osm", "--overwrite"
  ),
  envname = "osmnx-env"
)
```

## Step 3 — Build the Street Graph and Identify Intersections

The filtered file was loaded with OSMnx's `graph_from_xml()` to build one street network graph for the whole county. Only the largest connected part of the network was kept (`retain_all = FALSE`), which removes small, disconnected fragments. The graph was projected to a local metric coordinate system with `project_graph()`.

Intersections were then identified with `consolidate_intersections()`. A single real-world intersection is often represented in OSM by several nodes — for example, where a divided road meets a cross street. This function merges nodes that lie within 10 meters of each other (the OSMnx default tolerance) into one point at their center. Dead ends (cul-de-sacs and other nodes connected to only one street) were excluded (`dead_ends = FALSE`). The resulting points were converted to longitude/latitude.

```r
G_drive <- ox$graph_from_xml("data/osm/cook_drive_network.osm", retain_all = FALSE)
G_drive <- ox$project_graph(G_drive)

intersections <- ox$consolidate_intersections(G_drive, rebuild_graph = FALSE, dead_ends = FALSE)

coords_df <- intersections$to_crs("EPSG:4326")$get_coordinates()
lon <- as.numeric(reticulate::py_to_r(coords_df$x$to_numpy()))
lat <- as.numeric(reticulate::py_to_r(coords_df$y$to_numpy()))

cook_intersections <- tibble::tibble(lon = lon, lat = lat)
```

## Step 4 — Assign Intersections to Study-Area Units

Each intersection point was spatially joined to the study-area geography (Chicago's 77 community areas and suburban Cook County municipalities of at least 4 square miles). Points outside a study-area unit were dropped. Each intersection carries the unit's `geoid`, `name` and `type`.

```r
cook_intersections_geo <- cook_intersections %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) %>%
  st_transform(crs = 3435)

study_area_intersections <- cook_intersections_geo %>%
  st_join(study_area) %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  st_make_valid() %>%
  st_as_sf()

st_write(study_area_intersections, "data/intersections/study_area_intersections.gpkg", delete_dsn = TRUE)
```

## Output

`data/intersections/study_area_intersections.gpkg` is a point layer with one record per street intersection in the study area (about 170,000 points), in Illinois State Plane East (EPSG:3435), with the study-area attributes `geoid`, `name` and `type`. It is the source of the intersection sample used to compare crosswalk measurement methods ([`phase01_crosswalk_models.html`](phase01_crosswalk_models.html)).

## Limitations

- **OSM completeness.** Results depend on how completely and accurately roads are mapped and tagged in OSM. Missing or mistagged roads produce missing or extra intersections.
- **Data snapshot.** The dataset reflects the OSM extract on the date it was downloaded. Re-running the steps with a new extract updates it.
- **Merging tolerance.** The 10-meter tolerance may merge two closely spaced intersections into one, or leave a very large intersection split into more than one point.
